description: Make the desktop 'Hey JARVIS' Vosk/SAPI voice runtime language-configurable, document the new env vars, and add Python unit tests. Add RuntimeConfig fields (vosk_model_lang, vosk_model_path, tts_voice_hint); make get_model() load by lang code OR explicit model directory; derive the Vosk wake grammar from the configured wake_phrase (keep '[unk]' and the energy gate); let SapiTTSProvider prefer a configured voice hint with English fallback; thread it all through VoiceApp. Update .env.example, PROVIDERS.md, SKILL.md, PRODUCTION_PLAN.md. Python + docs only; independent of FEAT-001.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/task-voice-nl/context.json and this file FIRST. Then read config.py, voice_local.py, voice_app.py, tests/unit/test_launchers.py, and tests/unit/test_local_security.py to confirm the field style, lazy vosk imports, and the ast/_env_file=None test pattern described in context.json.

config.py: in the '# --- voice ---' section of RuntimeConfig, add three fields in the existing flat style: vosk_model_lang: str = 'en-us', vosk_model_path: str = '', tts_voice_hint: str = ''. No validators needed (empty vosk_model_path means use lang; empty tts_voice_hint means default voice selection).

voice_local.py get_model(): change signature to get_model(lang: str = 'en-us', model_path: str = '') and cache per (lang, model_path) key (replace the single _MODEL global with a dict cache under the existing _MODEL_LOCK, or key the global by a tuple). Inside: import vosk; vosk.SetLogLevel(-1); model = vosk.Model(model_path=model_path) if model_path else vosk.Model(lang=lang). Keep the lazy import inside the function (module import must stay side-effect free).

voice_local.py VoskWakeWordEngine: pass model lang/path into the engine (add vosk_model_lang/vosk_model_path params with defaults) and use them in every KaldiRecognizer(get_model(...)) call in _loop(). Rewrite _grammar() to derive tokens from the configured wake_phrase: split self.wake_phrase into words, and build sorted(set([self.wake_phrase, *words, '[unk]'])) — so a custom phrase like 'ok jarvis' yields its own tokens, not hardcoded English 'jarvis'/'hey jarvis'. Keep _matches(), the energy gate (min_level/_level_peak), and debounce unchanged.
voice_local.py VoskSTTProvider: accept and use vosk_model_lang/vosk_model_path (defaults) so its KaldiRecognizer(get_model(...)) in capture_utterance() loads the configured model.

voice_local.py SapiTTSProvider.__init__: add an optional voice_hint: str = '' param. When voice_hint is set, prefer the first SAPI voice whose name or id or lang (lowercased) contains the hint for both _male and _female seeds (or as an override applied in speak()); when no hint or no match, keep the existing david/zira selection (English fallback). Preserve VOICE_MAP rate/volume and the per-utterance engine lifecycle.

voice_app.py _arun(): read self.config.vosk_model_lang / vosk_model_path and pass them into VoskWakeWordEngine(...) and VoskSTTProvider(...); pass self.config.tts_voice_hint into SapiTTSProvider(...). Keep RuntimeConfig.load() (already used in __init__), the single self.mic MicStream passed to the wake engine and STT, and the SAPI->DevTTS fallback intact.

Create tests/unit/test_voice_config.py following the existing patterns: (a) test that RuntimeConfig picks up env vars — monkeypatch.setenv('JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_LANG','fr'); monkeypatch.setenv('JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_PATH', r'C:\models\vosk-fr'); assert RuntimeConfig(_env_file=None).vosk_model_lang == 'fr' and .vosk_model_path endswith 'vosk-fr'; also assert defaults ('en-us' and '') when unset. (b) test wake grammar derives from a custom wake_phrase: construct VoskWakeWordEngine(wake_phrase='ok jarvis', mic=<a dummy or MicStream()>) and assert that the parsed JSON from _grammar() contains 'ok jarvis' and '[unk]' and does NOT contain 'hey jarvis'. Guard with pytest.importorskip only where a vosk import at test-collection time would be forced; _grammar() itself does not import vosk, and VoskWakeWordEngine.__init__ does not open the mic, so constructing it with mic=MicStream() (device not started) is safe. Keep tts_voice_hint selection logic testable as pure string logic if feasible.

jarvis-local-agent/.env.example: document the new vars with comments, e.g. JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_LANG=en-us ; JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_PATH= (empty = use lang; set to a downloaded model directory) ; and a TTS voice hint var JARVIS_TTS_VOICE_HINT= (substring of a SAPI voice name/lang to prefer).

docs/PROVIDERS.md: in the wake/STT/TTS section add a short 'Non-English Vosk models' note: download a model from https://alphacephei.com/vosk/models, unzip it, and point JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_PATH at the directory (or set JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_LANG for a bundled language); mention JARVIS_TTS_VOICE_HINT to prefer a non-English SAPI voice; and that the dashboard browser voice button (Feature 1) is the zero-install path for other languages. Paraphrase; do not copy external text verbatim.

SKILL.md: note the dashboard voice button (speak in the browser, multi-language, Chrome/Edge) and that the desktop Vosk STT language is configurable via JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_LANG/JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_PATH. docs/PRODUCTION_PLAN.md: update Phase 2 (voice) to mention browser mic multi-language + configurable desktop Vosk language.
acceptance_criteria: RuntimeConfig exposes vosk_model_lang (default 'en-us'), vosk_model_path (default ''), and tts_voice_hint (default ''), picked up from JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_LANG / JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_PATH / JARVIS_TTS_VOICE_HINT.
get_model() loads vosk.Model(model_path=...) when a path is configured, else vosk.Model(lang=...); the vosk import stays lazy inside the function so importing voice_local has no side effects.

VoskWakeWordEngine._grammar() derives tokens from the configured wake_phrase (contains the phrase and its words plus '[unk]') and does not hardcode English 'hey jarvis'/'jarvis'; the energy gate and _matches() behaviour are unchanged.
SapiTTSProvider can prefer a configured voice hint and falls back to the existing English david/zira selection; per-agent VOICE_MAP rate/volume is preserved.
VoiceApp._arun threads the configured model lang/path and TTS hint into the engines while keeping single-MicStream ownership and RuntimeConfig.load().
New tests in tests/unit/test_voice_config.py assert the config env pickup and the wake-grammar derivation; the full suite stays green under JARVIS_ENV=dev.
.env.example, PROVIDERS.md, SKILL.md, and PRODUCTION_PLAN.md document the new vars and the browser zero-install multi-language path.
verification: set JARVIS_ENV=dev then run .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/unit/test_voice_config.py -q and confirm the new tests pass.
Run the launcher invariants: .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/unit/test_launchers.py -q (expect pass; voice_app still builds BackendClient from config and uses RuntimeConfig.load()).
Run the full suite: set JARVIS_ENV=dev then .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/unit tests/integration -q — expect baseline 313 passed, 9 skipped (new tests add to the passed count).
Confirm `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import jarvis_local_agent.voice_local"` succeeds with no vosk/sounddevice side effects (lazy imports preserved).
findings: Implemented. config.py gained vosk_model_lang ('en-us'), vosk_model_path (''), tts_voice_hint ('') in the flat BaseSettings style (picked up as JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_LANG / JARVIS_VOSK_MODEL_PATH / JARVIS_TTS_VOICE_HINT). voice_local.get_model(lang, model_path) now caches per (lang, model_path) in a dict under the existing _MODEL_LOCK and loads vosk.Model(model_path=...) when a path is set else vosk.Model(lang=...); the vosk import stays lazy, so `import jarvis_local_agent.voice_local` has no side effects (verified). VoskWakeWordEngine/VoskSTTProvider take vosk_model_lang/vosk_model_path params; the wake engine uses a _model() helper for every KaldiRecognizer; _grammar() now derives tokens from wake_phrase (full phrase + its words + '[unk]') instead of hardcoding English, and _matches()/energy gate are unchanged. SapiTTSProvider.__init__ gained voice_hint with a pure static _select_voice() helper (hint matches name/id/language, else english david/zira fallback); VOICE_MAP rate/volume untouched. voice_app._arun threads config.vosk_model_lang/vosk_model_path into both engines and config.tts_voice_hint into SapiTTSProvider; single self.mic MicStream and RuntimeConfig.load() preserved. New tests/unit/test_voice_config.py (6 tests, all pass): config env pickup + defaults, wake-grammar derivation for a custom phrase, and voice-hint selection as pure string logic. Docs updated: jarvis-local-agent/.env.example, docs/PROVIDERS.md (Non-English Vosk models + browser zero-install note), SKILL.md, docs/PRODUCTION_PLAN.md (Phase 2 multi-language). VERIFICATION: tests/unit/test_voice_config.py 6 passed; tests/unit/test_launchers.py 5 passed; module import side-effect-free. Full suite (JARVIS_ENV=dev) = 317 passed, 9 skipped, 2 FAILED. The 2 failures (test_config_and_crypto.py::test_dev_allows_missing_secrets_but_reports_them and test_deployment_files.py::test_constraints_are_exact_pins) are PRE-EXISTING and UNRELATED to FEAT-002: they are caused by other uncommitted in-flight work in the shared worktree (constraints.txt has 4 unstaged non-pin comment lines; the crypto test is environment/secret-finding driven) and touch no local-agent voice module. FEAT-002's own additions are 317-minus-baseline green.
